verses.note: Hebrews calls Noah an heir of the righteousness that comes by faith (Hebrews 11:7), and Ezekiel names him with Daniel and Job as a model of righteousness (Ezekiel 14:14). His blamelessness is not sinlessness, as chapter 9 shows; it is wholehearted integrity before God.

Paul reads the verse as God counting a person righteous apart from works, since Abram was declared righteous before circumcision and before the law (Romans 4:3-11, Galatians 3:6). James cites it to show that such faith is proved in obedience (James 2:21-23). Protestants have usually read ‘credited’ as God reckoning a righteousness not one's own; Roman Catholic and Orthodox readers have stressed that God's reckoning also makes a person righteous. All agree that the verse puts God's promise and Abram's trust before any merit.
